title: Quantization-Induced Honesty Regression: Does Compressing a Model Make It More Sycophantic?

original_idea.body: Quantization-Induced Honesty Regression. Problem: whether quantization degrades honesty properties separately from accuracy is essentially unstudied. Direction: take one open model FP vs 8-bit/4-bit, run identical sycophancy-pressure, hint-injection, calibration probes, measure whether honesty metrics regress more than accuracy.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: quantization-induced honesty regression affects most cost-conscious deployments.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run existing honesty probes on FP vs quantized variants; single GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused FP-vs-quantized delta; near-dup of gen-3473.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected community-quantization honesty audit no lab is incentivized to run.

low_compute.reasoning: Quantized variants on single GPU, inference-only.

novelty.reasoning: Quantization effects on honesty specifically appear largely unstudied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Quantization effects on honesty/sycophancy specifically appear under-explored.
